utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Judge Kamenova has a very urgent personal commitment which will occupy her for the first session, but she will be back with us after the first break. We've decided it's in the interests of all and the interests of justice to continue in her absence; she's happy with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Radinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to tell the truth which you gave at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply right through your time with us giving evidence. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning again, General and Professor Radinovic. I would like to take up where we left off, which I believe was with Exhibit 5D1175 which we had started to talk about, the "odluka" map for the Voksa action, if I can have that back up on the screen. And while we're waiting for that, sir, generally speaking, can it be said, as you indicated for "zapovests" or decisions or orders that the "odluka" itself is also an act of command by the commander who is preparing it or drafting it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that, but it's very rarely that such document is drafted. It's usually part of the order, it's called schematic and it's an attachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in the case of an involvement of two or more units simultaneously all of the commanders of these units receive respective copies of the "odluka" map and "zapovest" which they then use to instruct their units on the role in the planned combat action?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, you're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... What do they receive in the field?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The schematic of the decision, "odluka," is drawn on the map so that the superior can approve it; once it's approved, it's used as a basis for planning action. But maps don't have to be made for subordinates, subordinates make their own maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At which level or which organ prepares the "odluka" maps, or sema [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Working maps, as a rule are kept in commands from regiment, brigade, and up, and they can be kept in the commands of independent battalions. And others, excuse me, make different sketches, improvised drawings of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 1175 which we now have in front of us. Am I correct that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, before you proceed with that, your very first question this morning was whether the "odluka" itself is an act of command. Now, did you mean the question to refer to the "odluka" itself or to the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I meant the "odluka" map, I apologise, so I guess I should ask that again of the witness to make sure that we're clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think he did understand it because I think that's how he understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But I'm confused because of the apparent lack of relationship between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I meant the map, so if we need the witness to clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I think he's assumed that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General Professor, if we look at 5D1175, am I correct that the portions are colour-coded on the map to distinguish between MUP and VJ units?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me have a look. I don't see this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can maybe zoom in on the middle left portion of the -- of the map, that might make it easier for the witness, and just up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me see the legend. Yes, yes, you can see it on the sketch that MUP forces are shown in blue and the army in red.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can direct your attention, sir, am I correct that the blue on this map is actually the UCK or OVK, the KLA, positions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the disposition, I would say yes. But on the legend, if you can raise it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... A little bit to get to the bottom of the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, yes. We see here that the forces of the 5th Detachment of MUP, blocking forces, I said they were blocking forces; the legend says that they are the forces of the MUP. I don't think this was done well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Maybe it isn't showing up on your monitor but the first part of the legenda says [no interpretation] and it shows a green-blue line with stripes on it. Is that the part of the legend that you're referring to relating to the MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you look on the map just above you see an orange set of lines around the KLA forces representing the battle group 72 and battle group 125-2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to look at Exhibit P1613 with you for a moment, and this is a "zapovest" dated 27 August 1998, and the upper left-hand corner specifies that it originates from the Komanda MUP-a, command of the MUP, and is labelled as a military secret, taking a look at this document. And if need be we can pause to have you look at the remaining page of it. Does this "zapovest," or order, comport to the form of a "zapovest" from the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this first paragraph looks like a first paragraph of a military "zapovest," order, because it speaks of the enemy. I can't see the rest, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the -- go specifically to page 4, item number 7 of this document, it should be the same in both the English and B/C/S according to my notes. And we see there under logistical support, I think on the English it goes on to page -- to the top of page 5 as well, so we might have to move the English for the English-speaking persons. Am I correct that the "zapovest" in question provides instructions for the VJ units in providing support to the MUP in this action, including the use of various types of munitions being authorised?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logistical support relies on garrisons, and in garrisons, in depots, weaponry is also in storage to support the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you look at the last paragraph of this order and last page which is entitled: "Command and communications," once we get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's the second-last page in English, I apologise, the translation does not follow the B/C/S completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, if we look at again the last paragraph of the order we see it says: [Interpretation] "Command forces from the forward command post in the area of Djakovica through the brigade commander." [Previous translation continues]... [In English] Knowledge and information of this of the operations of the VJ, are we talking about an -- when talking about an IKM, is that a military term and a military organ?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a place that the commander puts forward in order to command his units. It's a point from which command is exercised. Part of the command is located there so the command can function.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Signed and stamped the command of the Pristina Corps by the then-commander of the Pristina Corps General Pavkovic. Is -- in your opinion, is this a document originating from the command of the MUP or the command of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to tell you I'm seeing this document for the first time, but based on this one cannot conclude where it originates from, whether from MUP or the command of the Pristina Corps because there are two indications, one where it is filed, and the second who it is signed by. Both of them speak to the origin, so I'm confused by this document and I've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the existence of an organ called the Komanda MUP-a at any level?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of other organs of command, not the MUP command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can move to Exhibit 6D731, this is a document originating from the command of the 15th OKBR in Bijelo Polje dated August the 14th, 1998. First of all, is the organ sending this document as well as the recipient BG15/3, are they both VJ organs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a combat group of the 15th Armoured Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we focus on paragraph 2 of this order, I believe it's on the first page of both the B/C/S and the English, we see that BG15/3 is tasked with the 8th "odred" of the MUP to attack from the direction of Cesta, et cetera. This would be another example of the VJ being tasked to provide more than merely logistical and fire support to the MUP in an action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the last page of this document, and again specifically the last line before the signature and seal of Colonel Cirkovic, of the VJ, it says I believe we'll see shortly in the B/C/S that the overall command of this anti-terrorist action is at the level of the Pristina Corps command from its IKM and that they command and lead all forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would comport with your earlier conclusion that the VJ cannot be commanded by a MUP officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the Army of Yugoslavia was not commanded by a MUP officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gist of this document is in paragraph 4, you can look it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's move back to -- page 1 I believe it's section 4 if I'm not mistaken. I don't have the document in front of me to verify that, but I think we can get there quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that the part you wanted to refer to, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can just bring it closer up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Bottom section of the B/C/S document, please. It's already focused on the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what did you wish to point out to us with respect to this section?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in section 4, decision, I have decided, we see point 4.1, fourth line down: "Objective of the attack: To support MUP forces in destroying," et cetera. So the basic task of the units is to support MUP forces, and that's why the commander orders it and signs it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think that's it for this document. If we can move still to 1998, Exhibit 3D697, and first of all I would ask since this is a different form of document I would ask that the first page be shown, and I would ask if you can tell us what kind of a document this is. Please bear with me, General, we'll get the document up in a second. It takes some time sometimes for the documents to load. This one is a larger one. Now, General Professor, if you look at the first page of this document which we do have in B/C/S, does this appear to be a post-operation analysis done in October of 1998 by the 3rd Army relating to the relation of assignments on the territory of Kosovo-Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can move and focus on section 2.2 on the next page of the document in both the B/C/S and the English, it's at the bottom in the B/C/S if we can focus on the bottom three paragraphs. And it's going to be actually the next page on the English it would appear, page 3 of the English. It's going to be the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you could take a few moments to review this portion of the report and tell us in summation the activities of the units specified as well as their interaction with one another, if this shows again that the MUP and the VJ jointly operated during these assignments on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me to read the whole page or a certain portion?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 2.2 [no interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2.2 implementation of tasks, 2.2, so it is a list. The first task is to secure the state border, then goes an explanation, and the second task is to engage forces in the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 3 and 4 on the next page talk about the participation of MUP and VJ units. I would like to move ahead to attachment 3 of this document which is on -- at the end -- I think the third- or fourth-to-last page of this exhibit to ask about the specific personnel involved in these actions to see about the -- if we can shed some light on the methodology of this report. In -- while we're waiting to get there, General, in your report you rely upon certain statistics about the number of personnel from the MUP and the VJ that were utilised in these anti-terrorist actions in 1998; am I correct, the total number of personnel?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it's not even that precise. These are rough data.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can take a look at attachment number 3, we have it on the English and we're getting it on the B/C/S. First of all, with respect to the SAJ and the JSO -- we're not on that part of the attachment yet on the B/C/S, but I'll -- I think I can start with my --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see no other picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The introductory part of my analysis while we wait for the document to come up on the screen in B/C/S. When talking about the MUP having one SAJ and one JSO unit in its structure, would that be fair to say was the case in both 1998 and 1999, was there one SAJ unit and one JSO unit in the structure of the MUP as evident from their very name themselves [B/C/S spoken], we're talking about a structure existing one unit each, would you agree with that, as you stated in your report?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, again we're trying to locate the appropriate page in the B/C/S. There we have it now, sir. Hopefully now, General, you can see the [B/C/S spoken] consisting of a chart listing the personnel involved from both the MUP and the VJ for these actions in 1998. Now, first of all, as far as the methodology of this chart is concerned, the methodology behind the creation of this chart is concerned, if we look at the columns for the SAJ and the JSO which are in the middle of the document, we see that the number of units involved in these actions for the SAJ is reported as eight and for the JSO is reported as three. Now, given that we're in agreement that there's only one unit of each of these formations, for purposes of this chart can we conclude that where the same unit participated in multiple operations that same unit was counted multiple times for each time that it participated in operation. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that what you are suggesting as an answer is correct. There was a unit for special operations, JSO, as one unit, whereas special anti-terrorist units existed in several places, in Belgrade, Novi Sad, Pristina, and there was a number of them. So I would be more inclined to accept this as correct rather than your suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. How many JSO units were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And on this chart it shows three JSO units were engaged in operations. Would you agree that that tends to indicate that the same JSO unit was counted multiple times?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these were parts of that unit. One of the groups of that unit would be involved in each of these operations because if these are minor operations, then the JSO doesn't have to be used as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Could participate in more than one operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot participate in more than one operation if they were close in time, one after another, then the unit would have to be separated into different groups and used along several axes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Is it possible that the same units participated in multiple operations?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that they participated in multiple operations because we don't have the timing of the operations here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, am I correct that as part of your expertise you don't have precise knowledge as to the number and placement of MUP personnel in Kosovo-Metohija in 1999, that was not part of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not a part of the analysis to determine precisely the strength, but I know roughly and I stated it in my report, which kind of units, where, how, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to finish up 1998 and move on to another topic, yesterday you mentioned General Perisic as the commander of the army ought to know the utilisation of his forces. If we look at 3D757, this is -- and specifically page 5 of the English and page 6 of the B/C/S, I believe here we have General Perisic talking about the VJ in the operations in 1998, saying that they had the leading role in these operations, the "nosela aksija" [phoen] a term you've used. Now, I would ask you -- we have to wait again for the documents, sir, I apologise, it's page 5 of the English and page 6 of the B/C/S. It's at the bottom -- the bottom -- the second-to-last paragraph on the B/C/S that's visible now, don't go down, it's right in the middle of the page now. [Interpretation] The VJ carried out all tasks fully, professionally, and play the main role in operations against sabotage groups." [In English] General, all the documents we've gone through, particularly General Perisic's comments here, could you agree with me that your conclusion we started off our discussion with in your report at paragraph 90 that the MUP played the leader -- and the MUP leadership played the lead role in these anti-terrorist actions, that that is an oversimplification of a complex situation that will would need to be analysed based upon each particular operation, each particular task in each operation. Would you agree with me in that regard?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would agree with you only in part that it is important all of this be analysed from one detail to the other, but in that case my report would have been 5.000 pages long, not 200, and I would have had to spend far more resources on that. As for the level that I was working at, I think that that was unnecessary. I did not deal with a multitude of details contained in your question. However, when I claimed that the anti-terrorist operation was carried out in coordination by the army and the police and that the prevailing role was played by the MUP forces, that is quite certain, although General Perisic in this summary document that reviews what had been done states that the army played the decisive role where the combat activities, or rather, where combat operations were involved in dealing with terrorists. When the army and the police meet in the same area, then it is the military officer who is in charge and who brings this together. That is the way it is according to the law and according to military doctrine, because they are better-versed in such things than the police. Because for the police, combat action is not their primary task although they are trained for that, but this is not their primary activity. So when planning and implementation of combat activity is required, then it is only natural that it is commanders and officers at lower levels that deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The Law of Defence. We have a copy of the Law of Defence at P985, and I would like to start our discussion relating to Article 16 of the Law on Defence this is page 2 of the B/C/S version and page 3 of the English version of P985; and looking at Article 16 which in summation says that the Army of Yugoslavia is the organizer of the armed struggle and shall unite all participants in the armed struggle and command all combat activities, I believe that relates to what you have just said. And I would ask you with respect to Article 16, as an expert, can you tell us if your understanding of Article 16 is that automatically upon the declaration of a state of war the VJ assumes the role of uniting and commanding all friendly forces engaged in combat activities. And I think this is something that you have discussed at paragraph 151 of your report, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 16 of the law is geared towards the role of the army in defending the country from an external enemy, external aggression. However, regrettably, we - I mean Yugoslavia and Serbia - were waging a so-called internal war, there wasn't an external enemy, I'm talking about 1998, not 1999, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead finish first.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, in a way, it could be perplexing if 1998 were to be projected within Article 16 and the role of the army. Obviously it does not pertain to that reality. Article 16 certainly pertains to 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Correction or clarification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one second. I wonder if you could speak more directly into the microphone, please, Mr. Radinovic to assist the interpretation. And Mr. Ivetic, my paragraph 151 has nothing to do with this. Was that the correct reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 151, at least on my copy at page 117 says that the basis for that order is in Article 16 of the Law on Defence which is the article we're looking at right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, it's the page number that's the problem, 117, that's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There might be two paragraphs about that, I'm not positive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to combat operations that would fall under Article 16, Article 16 would also apply to the relations between the MUP and the VJ, is that correct, as far as combat operations are concerned?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we can look at Exhibit P1981 briefly, I think we can do that one in one question if I phrase it properly. This is a "zapovest" of the command of the 549th Motorised Brigade of the VJ dated 23 March 1999, and if we look at section 4 of this document, which is the section you have told us is the one to look at for purposes of analysis of the units involved, I think we will see again that the VJ commander is giving instructions to his units to work together with the MUP units. Given that this order predates the order on resubordination, can we conclude that Article 16 is being employed of the Law of Defence for purposes of giving these instructions? Would it be logical?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're asking me. I am not asserting at all that the MUP and the army did not act together. That's not what I said in my report. That's not what I'm saying now. The question is only what the relationship involved is. Is it cooperation, coordination, or command? It's not one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to resubordination as the next topic. You in your report give reasons for the issuance of the various orders on resubordination, specifically at paragraphs 152 and 153, including the fears of a NATO ground invasion and the strained relationship between the Republic of Montenegro and the rest of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which led to an effort to try and have the MUP of Montenegro subordinated to the command of the 2nd Army as you state. Now, would you agree with me and my interpretations of your conclusions as set forth in paragraph 157 of your report that the VJ did not have the same problems with the MUP of Serbia that it had with the MUP of Montenegro over the imposition of Article 17 of the Law of Defence on resubordination?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you that it did not have the same problems like with the MUP of Montenegro, because the MUP of Montenegro obstructed the army's efforts in defending the country. The MUP of Serbia did not do that, on the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to paragraph -- paragraphs 144 to 145 of your report and paragraph 148 of the same, when dealing with Article 17 of the Law of Defence and the order of the president of the FRY on resubordination of the MUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I see Mr. Stamp on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think probably this is the same thing, P1981 is from the record in e-court a document which is under seal. On the face of it I can't imagine why, but I think it might have in it the name or names of protected persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we've moved on to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We've moved on and we didn't look at the document in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- So the position is noted and we shall proceed to the next matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, General, let me start again. At paragraphs 144 to 145 of your report and at paragraph 148 you discuss Article 17 and the order of the president of the FRY regarding resubordination of the MUP, and you state that it relates to only units carrying out combat actions or combat operations, "borbeni dejstva" this is also something that General Kosovac confirmed. Would you therefore agree with me that resubordination under Article 17 of the Law on Defence did not apply to all other jobs and functions of the MUP, such as traffic control, criminal investigations, crime prevention, issuance of identity documents, et cetera, and that these functions remained under the purview and authority of the MUP and its subordinate SUPs and OUPs?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And another thing that General Kosovac testified about was that there was some confusion regarding the implementation of resubordination, and I'd like to take a few minutes to review two documents with you that we have already introduced into evidence the first is 6D117, which is an order from the VTO, Vojno-Teritorijalni Odred, from Istok which -- in which the VTO commander attempts to -- if we can have the document -- there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if I may just interrupt a moment to note that Judge Kamenova has now joined us on the Bench, and I do that for the record. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is an order from the VTO Istok where the commander of the VTO attempts to take over control of various functions in the municipality, including placing the commander of the SUP subordinate to him. Would such an action be in compliance with the spirit and letter of Article 17 or President Milosevic's order on resubordination, specifically items 1 of this order and item 2 and sub-item 4 under item 2 of this order, if you can briefly skim through those?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is barely legible. Could it please be zoomed in a bit because there's also ... Could you please lower it a bit, a bit more -- actually, could you scroll up, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I think that's what the General was asking for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to see the beginning of the document, right, yeah. Yes, that would do. Look at this, commander of the 69th Military Territorial Detachment in the preamble invokes the order of the supreme commander. This is inconceivable in military communication, that the commander of the detachment invokes the order of the supreme commander. He should only invoke the order made by his superior officer. This shows you what the quality of this document is. It certainly does not pertain to the order of the 18th of April on the resubordination of forces in terms of what this commander is asking for; that is to say, it's not that the MUP secretariats should be resubordinated for carrying out their regular work, what was referred to in the original order was combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Number 1 of the order appears to attempt to place all republican and opstina leadership under the command of the VTO Istok. Would you agree that that too is an over -- going overboard as far as Article 16 or Article 17 of Law of Defence are concerned?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just briefly, I think since it's a related document 6D125, which is an order from the Vojno-Teritorijalni Odred, VTO, of Pec, and again if you could take a few moments to review that document, do we again have a situation where the commander of this VTO is not in compliance with the Law of Defence and is going overboard in terms of what he is seeking from various organs in the "opstina" level, including the SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously he didn't understand. He does not understand the question. He does not understand the problem. He is asking for things that he is not entitled to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can just ask you about one more hypothetical example. Does the Article 17 of the Law of Defence and the order of the president of the FRY resubordination, does it oversee the assistant ministers of interior and the chiefs of all SUPs in non-combat areas sitting at the command of the army level and resubordinating themselves to the commander of the army, for instance, the 2nd Army, which was not in a combat zone for the most part?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That does not mean that these police officers should sit with military commanders, even if it has to do with areas of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 158 of your report you base your conclusion that the MUP of Serbia did not comply with the order of the FRY president on resubordination. You base this upon a combat report of the 3rd Army dated 20 April 1999. Now, we have heard testimony that the Supreme Command Staff did not send any orders to the Ministry of the Interior, I think you've also stated that somewhere in our report. And if we look at the order of the 3rd Army on resubordination, it only goes to the commander of the PJP. Now, if we can look at Exhibit P1267, this is the order at the level of the Pristina Corps command, and I think reading it you'll see that it comes the closest to complying with the spirit and letter of Article 17 of the Law of Defence where -- because it limits itself to units and formations in combat actions. Now if we look at this document, it is dated the 20th of April, 1999, and in its text it says that the order on resubordination is to be implemented by the 25th of April, 1999. Would you agree with me that based upon this document the April 20th, 1999, combat report of the 3rd Army becomes moot insofar as the MUP hadn't yet received any order on resubordination, in fact had until the 25th of April to implement it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot accept what you are offering to me as an answer for a simple reason. The order of the president, or rather, the supreme commander and chief of the VSO dated the 18th of April, and this is dated the 20th of April, that means that they still haven't received the former. It is certain that the order was not carried through and the army commander is right when he asks for that to be carried out. Now, whether it was possible to do that within that time-frame is something that we can debate now, but obviously that is not the way it was carried out and it is not surprising at all that he asked for this on the 20th, to have this order carried through.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, General, the order from the president of the FRY, which you have I believe reproduced the text of in your report at item 2, says that the chief of the Supreme Command Staff is to undertake actions to realise the order. And we've heard testimony from several persons at the level of the Supreme Command Staff that no such actions were taken by the Supreme Command Staff. Does that change your opinion as to whether we can conclude that the MUP received the order on resubordination prior to the 20th of April, which is the date of this document from General Lazarevic of the Pristina Corps, advising the MUP of the resubordination -- he's advising the MUP staff of the resubordination and giving a date of April the 25th for its realisation. Would you agree with me that the combat report of the 20th of April by the 3rd Army is not the complete picture, given this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as for the command report of the commander of the 3rd Army dated the 20th of April in which the commander asks for the realisation of the order of the supreme commander on resubordinating the MUP forces is something that I understand as insight into the situation on that day, the 20th of April, and no doubt that it hadn't been carried through on that date, the 20th of April. You put several questions as you were speaking. You asked me whether the Supreme Command Staff had taken all necessary measures for the realisation. They did everything that was within the realm of their responsibility, and the commander of the Pristina Corps is not supposed to issue an order on the resubordination of MUP forces in Kosovo. It should be done by the vertical chain of the MUP, from the top to the MUP units in Kosovo or the staff in Kosovo. So the units of the MUP should have gotten this order down their own chain, that they will be resubordinated in combat operations to army units, that is, then coordination is organized, then things are coordinated, and then they're done properly. The commander of the VSO saw that that was not happening and he asked for that to be carried through, and it is not the obligation of the chief of the Supreme Command Staff to send orders to the minister of the interior. He is not subordinated to him. He did not have that kind of obligation. It's not surprising that he didn't send an order to him, and why the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia did not send it through his lines of command and control. And whether he did it at all, I don't know, obviously not since the resubordination did not take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm losing the thread of this, I'm afraid, Mr. Ivetic, because we're jumping around I think from issue to issue. Mr. Radinovic, if an order of the general nature of the one that was made here about resubordination of MUP forces is made by the supreme commander, how should that be relayed to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The supreme commander has his military office, military cabinet, that serves him in terms of all kinds of communication with organs that are outside the army. The order that he issued was supposed to be addressed to the Government of Serbia, and then the Government of Serbia to the minister of the interior, the minister of the interior down his vertical chain of command to units in Kosovo and Metohija. That is the way it was supposed to be done. I assume --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On a separate question now, in this document on the screen, if you look at paragraph 5 there is a reference to the 25th of April, and the point Mr. Ivetic is, I think, making to you is that it's hardly open to the commander of the 3rd Army to complain about failure to act on an instruction about resubordination on the 20th of April when apparently the deadline for doing this was the 25th of April. Now, what's your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assume that the commander of the 3rd Army was in contact with the MUP officers and that he knew that they had not received any orders on resubordination. So, in fact, there was no resubordination and that is why he appealed to the Supreme Command Staff to have this carried through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And there's a bit of speculation involved there, obviously, on your part. But where in that scenario does this date of the 25th of April fit in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an order issued by the commander of the Pristina Corps, who is subordinate to the command of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, but he's part of the 3rd Army, and presumably the complaint by the commander of the 3rd Army is because -- is made because things are not working further down the line, and this is an example of an order made further down the line which gave a different deadline.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the way I understand it as follows: This was not done by the 12th [as interpreted], so a new deadline was set up to the 25th. I have no other explanation to give.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that explanation any more than speculation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's not much of an explanation, but I have no other explanation to give. There's no other explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just to close out one more area on this. The order of the FRY president is Exhibit 3D670, you cite to it in your report and actually cite the text of it at paragraph 154 of your report on page 118. If we can have that exhibit, 3D670, up on the screen just briefly, I would like to focus on item 2 of the order and obtain the witness's comments relating upon reading that directive. Could you focus on the directing in paragraph 2 of this order which states that the chief of the Supreme Command Staff will regulate by his order all other matters arising from item 1 of this order, item 1 being the invocation of Article 17 on the Law on Defence. Would you agree with me that this order places an obligation upon the Supreme Command Staff to order -- to effectuate orders to implement Article 17?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but within the scope of its competence, not beyond it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And item 3 of this order indicates the chief of the Supreme Command Staff should send requests to civilian government organs and other defence bodies. Those would not normally be subordinate to him, would they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they wouldn't be. This is not an order, it's a request. He's requesting that such and such be done. He's requesting this of the organs of civilian defence, of the civilian authorities, those who he feels ought to support the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Article 1 -- pardon me, item 1 of this order deals exclusively with the MUP, with the units of the interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the units of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And item 2 incorporates item 1 as being the basis for the instruction from the president of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an order, or rather, item 2 of this order, the chief of the supreme defence staff shall regulate through his order all other matters arising from item 1 of this order, so everything that pertains to the army. If you look at item 3, that's his request to others who are not part of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem for me with that, Mr. Radinovic, is the answer you gave earlier that the responsibility for that communication lay with the military cabinet of the president rather than with the normal military command structure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the supreme commander, when communicating along the vertical chain of command with the army, has his Supreme Command Staff. It's not necessary to explain that here because it's been mentioned so often, and the Supreme Command Staff covers this kind of communication fully. However, it does not cover communication with other government organs; this is done through the military cabinet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. So why does paragraph 3 here put the obligation on the chief of the Supreme Command Staff to send his request to the civilian government organs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 3 which mentions the civilian authorities and organs refers to what these organs should provide for the best possible operation of the army, so this refers to various forces, various resources at the level of the state which should be acting in unison in order for the action to be as efficient as possible. And these requests for everything that is necessary to support the action, the supreme commander ordered the chief of the Supreme Command Staff to take measures to achieve this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one matter to deal with in the transcript. Page 24, line 11, the date the 12th should, in fact, be the 20th. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can focus on the time-period after the 25th of April, 1999, am I correct that there were anti-terrorist actions undertaken jointly by elements of the MUP and the VJ after that date?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just for the sake of clarity, anti-terrorist actions of the nature undertaken in 1999 would be considered combat actions under the military definition of that term; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-terrorist actions, yes, conditionally speaking because it's on the borderline between military and police operations, and therefore without analysing each particular case it's very hard to say what predominates. Is it a fight against terrorism or is it a fight against armed groups in combat operations. However, in principle I would agree with your statement, these are primarily combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We're waiting for the transcript to catch up. Now, with respect to these actions, they were undertaken pursuant to "zapovests" and "odlukas" prepared by the VJ commanders at the -- in their areas of responsibility; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Article 17 is complied with and all the orders, then the answer is yes; if not, then the answer is no. There is information, and this can be seen in the documents as well, that the resubordination did not function properly, which doesn't mean that at the lower level there was no coordination, of course there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Documents that I have as a sample of some of the actions post-dating the 25th of April. If you look at the "zapovest" for the action Sekac [phoen] which is -- which is -- one moment, I have to find the number for that, I somehow skipped that, P2011, and we're going to be looking at part 5 of the order, which is the instructions to the units, which is on page 2 to 3 of the B/C/S, the bottom of 2 and the top of 3. And I believe it's the same in the English, I'll find out as soon as the document comes up on the screen. Looking at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Maybe we better start at the first page to do this in a logical manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Looking at the first page, can you identify the source of this "zapovest," the organ that is promulgating it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Pristina Corps from the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the date is the 20th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we see that the location is Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can now turn to page 2 of the B/C/S, the bottom, and the witness will need to be shown pages 2 and 3 of the document, the [B/C/S spoken], item 5, and on the English I think it's actually going to be page 3 rather than 2, based on what we had come up on the screen just a few moments ago. Well, it looks like it's actually going to be the next page in the English, there we go, tasks of the units beginning on page 4 of the English and leading over on to page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir - and you'll take the time to glance through this section - that the "zapovest" gives very precise instructions to both VJ and MUP units that were to be involved in this action?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if you look at the last page of the document, I think we can confirm that it was, in fact, signed by Colonel Milan Kotur, an officer within the Pristina Corps during the relevant time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it's the second-last page of the English since the last page is blank.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the item on command and communication, can you conclude whether the command post identified is a VJ or a MUP structure?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's within the Army of Yugoslavia, the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to P1503 and we'll look at the first page of this document briefly. This is, I believe, the "zapovest" for the action in Prekaz dated May 27th, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, is this document originating from the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the title of the document, do we see that it's being directed to the MUP, albeit the Komanda MUP, which you testified about earlier you did not hear of such an organ existing?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again if we could turn to section 5, the instructions to the units, this is at page 3 of the B/C/S and hopefully page 3 of the English, although for some reason we didn't have luck on the last document -- page 4 of the English I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this document also gives instructions for both MUP and VJ units for the undertaking of this combat operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the brigade commander is issuing tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn to the last page of the document and look at the last line of section 14 we see, once we get there I think we'll see -- well, I think the second-to-last page in English is necessary because it cuts off the paragraph in the half, but I think we'll see that the document identifies that the command of the 37th Motorised Brigade is in charge of leading this operation. And I think you would agree that that would comport with the proper level at which resubordination would take place, as set forth in paragraphs 148 and 149 of your report. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 14 talks about joint action between elements of the combat organization in the Prekaz area and the command of the 37th Brigade shall organize this. So the brigade is planning the combat operation and its commander is responsible for cooperation. He has to organize the cooperation. Joint action and cooperation is not one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the next document I would like to go through, I think it's 6D712.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before -- just before you move on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Line 14 it should be: Coordinated action, not joint action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, well that helps to remove the confusion, I think. Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry, I'm sorry. Page 30, line 16, joint action and cooperation is not one and the same thing, but I think that the witness said: [No interpretation] [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said: Coordinated action, joint action, and command, not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, General, we're in agreement that the operation was planned by the commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was -- he received orders to plan the operation. He was ordered to plan the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next document we have is 6D712, a "zapovest" and "odluka" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry to intervene again, at line 13 there one of the things you said was item 14 talks about joint action between elements of the combat organization in the Prekaz area and the command of the 37th Brigade shall organize this. That's an accurate translation of what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document 6D712 we don't have an English translation for, so I'll try to be brief on it and touch on the points and have the witness confirm. This is this -- once we get it up on the screen this will be the "zapovest" for Drenica 1, and I would focus the attention on the first page, first of all, once we get that up on the screen -- oh, it is up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to this document dated May the 28th, again the source or originating organ for this order is the command of the Pristina Corps, and it is directed to the MUP or at least the Komanda MUP, according to the title of the document; would you agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see. To the command of the MUP for -- I can't see what it says here, it's not legible. Can you read it if you have the original copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Does that appear to be the -- okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yes, for all --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- Of -- well, actually, I think we've gone through several documents already to short-circuit this. Since we don't have a translation, I would submit that item 5 likewise has similar language to the last two orders, identifying tasks for both MUP and VJ units. And I think once the document is translated it will -- that part will speak for itself. And I would like to then move to the "odluka" map, which is the last page of the exhibit, and I think that's just in the B/C/S -- in the -- it's not in colour since we've been having some difficulties of getting colour copies of maps from the Government of Serbia, but hopefully we can make some use of the map itself in its black-and-white form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where the original map still exists, and the indications have been given earlier in this case that they do, then the originals really should be produced. These are very important documents in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I've requested them several months ago from the Government of Serbia, and I'm still trying to work on that and effectuate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps what has just been said may be communicated to them because the absence of the originals impairs our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will do my best to make sure they are apprised of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General Professor, if we look at this map from 1999, this action for the Drenica activities, does it comport to the same format for the map of 1998 that we saw, that is to say that the organ responsible for drawing up the map is identified at the bottom right and the organ approving the action is identified at the upper left of this map? And if we need to zoom in on a portion, please let me know, I'd be more than happy to oblige.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct in what I've just said?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in both cases the organs involved are VJ organs, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this map, if we look at the formations listed --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the 37th Motorised Brigade, the 15th Armoured Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at the bottom -- just above the legenda, we see a notation for the 252nd Okupla [phoen] Brigada, and if you zoom in on that, I think, the subscript indicates that the 122nd Intervention Brigade of the MUP is also part of this action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Left, to the left, please, the left side of the document should be showing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There, General, at the lower left corner of the screen before you I believe we have an indication that the MUP unit is involved; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then if we go to the right-hand side under the tactical group of the 252nd, I think we have the -- that's the upper right, there we go, TG in Cyrillic 252, we have the either the 50th or the 30th "odred" of the PJP; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you expect, although we don't have this in colour, based on your knowledge and experience, would you expect the forces and their basic tasks to be colour-coded on the map based on the custom and practice of preparing maps for actions in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I would expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I promise I was going to try and short-circuit this and I have one more area to go to so I would like to just propose, and I'm sure that the other counsel will correct me if I'm wrong, but Exhibits P2014 and 6D707 are two other similar documents relating to actions after the 25th of April, 1999, and I think we have a translation of one but not of the other. But the item 5 of those speaks I think for itself as to the units that are given instructions. And I will represent to you, sir, and I think it's clear that the MUP and the VJ units are instructed in that section. Given the documents that we've gone through, would you agree with these are all combat actions planned by the VJ and at least overseen and commanded by brigade commanders of the VJ relating to activities of the VJ and the MUP, as stated in the "zapovest"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can just briefly turn to some of the documents -- the few documents that talk about complaints relating to interaction between the MUP and the VJ, are you familiar with 3D692, which is a report dated the 25th of May, 1999, by General Velickovic arising out of the control inspection of the Pristina Corps? Are you aware of such an inspection taking place in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Once we get that document on the screen I'll ask for page 4, item 11 in both versions. And, General, while we're waiting for that I will reveal what I'm asking you with respect to this. In this -- in this report there is a complaint against the MUP in relation to salaries and privileges enjoyed by the MUP that the VJ conscripts were upset about. Now, am I correct, sir, that insofar as you did not deal in detail with the MUP in this report, that you are not in a position to state any conclusions relating to the laws and regulations relating to compensation of the members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I assumed. And in any event, Article 17 does not relate to salaries, equipment, et cetera, of respective forces, either the VJ or the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say no, does that mean that Article 17 does not deal with that or ...

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. You asked me whether Article 17 deals with salaries and my answer was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we focus for a moment on Crisis Staffs. Based on your knowledge --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I still have ten minutes or more of questions, but I see we are at the one-and-a-half point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In light of that, we'll break now, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Radinovic, we need to have a break at this stage for a number of reasons. Could you leave with the usher and we'll see you again ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Hello again, General Professor Radinovic. Before we turn again to this exhibit we have on the screen, I wanted to ask you the question I started before the break that we had. If we focus for a moment on Crisis Staffs, based on your knowledge and expertise, am I correct that Articles 16 and 17 of the Law of Defence do not subordinate the MUP to Crisis Staffs at the local level?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I tried to follow, but I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me try and simplify it. Based upon your knowledge and expertise of Articles 16 and 17 of the Law of Defence, these articles do not mention or involve so-called Crisis Staffs, "Krizni Stabovi," in the subordination of the MUP at the local level?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we can return to this Exhibit 3D692, the report of the control carried out by General Velickovic, and if we can focus on item 11 which is now visible on both the B/C/S and the English on the screen, it indicates one of the findings being there as: "There is no single command over all the forces in the zone of responsibility. All contacts with the units of the MUP, Ministry of the Interior are established by agreement, which is often disobeyed, especially at the lower levels." Now, if we can look at item 12 which is just below item 11 on the same page, would you agree with me that the aforementioned problems or weaknesses are being experienced by, including various brigades, the 354th Brigade of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 37th, the 354th, this is about consequences on brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... At 5D506, this is a report that predates this report dated the 27th of April, 1999, from the command of the 354th Brigade. And I would like to obtain your comment on item 4(B) of this document, which should be on the first page once we get it up on the screen. Again, General, I ask your patience while we get the B/C/S up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd just like to perhaps request some guidance from you. How would you prefer that those of us who can't read B/C/S deal with these documents when there's no translation? I might have questions I want to ask about what's contained in these documents, and I know they can't be instantly translated for us. I don't bring this witness back at some future date, it makes no sense to me. I just don't know how you want us to deal with it, but I think there's some unfairness in it and I think there may well be something in this document I want to ask the witness about it. I don't know. It's a problem, I just don't know how to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think -- I understand the problem, Mr. Ackerman. I think one saving grace may be that it's not an exhibit of the sixth accused and that it's likely to crop up in the case of the fifth accused, by which time it hopefully will have been translated. What do you have to say on this, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we have been having difficulty getting our own documents translated, since CLSS is of the opinion we are sixth accused and I'm sure the fifth accused is in the same position, they are giving priority to prior defendants to translate documents. We have been trying to obtain an independent translator to assist with our documents we have problems with the registry now who first approved and is not wanting to approve that. So we are trying to work that out. I don't know what else to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you had that arrangement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We thought so as well, Your Honour. It's not as clear as it was--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you never been using your own independent --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have been using for our independent and now the registry is refusing to compensate for the services of the independent, so we're trying to work that out with the registry, but there are problems, I think, with everyone in terms of getting documents translated, given the way that the -- the number of the documents involved and the capacities of CLSS. As always, I look to the Trial Chamber for guidance on this. I am going to be asking the witness about exhibit -- about this exhibit, specifically paragraph 3(B), and if need be I can read into the record the entire paragraph. That's one way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think the present document can be dealt with that way, but this ties in with another matter which is currently exercising the minds of the Trial Chamber. It's counter-productive to spend a lot of time trying to work out exactly who is at fault in relation to every element of translation, but I think it's enough for us to say that we're not entirely satisfied that every accused has been making every effort to cooperate with the requests made by CLSS. And the further we go in this case, the more significant that failure to cooperate is likely to be. Now, we've invested a lot of time ourselves and a measure of our own credibility in seeking cooperation from CLSS, and we are very gratified at the response we've had in doing that. But I think it's fair to say that when they've made requests of some counsel here, they have not always had full cooperation from counsel. So against that background there are two matters that are currently issues, and the first is the motion by Lazarevic to amend the Rule 65 ter list to include documents not previously included, and this may well be one of them. A number of these have not been translated. Now, the time is up for the Prosecution response to this and their complaint is they can't make a meaningful response without having the English translations. The inclination of the Bench would be, therefore, to reject all the untranslated documents and leave it to the Lazarevic Defence to make a further application once they've been translated. The problem with that is highlighted by the current situation. If this particular document, 3D506, is one of these, then obviously we have to deal with it separately as an individual case as it arises in court. The other difficulty is that the Prosecution may have comments to make about the ones which have, in fact, been translated and haven't submitted any response as yet. Now, Mr. Stamp, do you have any opposition to any of the Lazarevic documents which have actually been translated into English?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Actually, we are not in a position to state whether or not we have any objections to those. We only got the CDs for all of these documents yesterday, so we have not been able to review --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that motion was filed on the 3rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, but we only got the CDs with the documents yesterday, so we have not had an opportunity to review these documents. And in fact, we had intended to ask today for an extension of the time to respond until Friday so that we could have an opportunity to have a look at these documents we just received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, you are -- Mr. Cepic, you undoubtedly are not entirely innocent in this whole debate, and I don't want to enter into a counter-productive exchange about that. But this is an example of the problem. So since the Prosecution are not in a position to respond, then what we will do is extend the time for them to respond, and since they only got the documents yesterday that could be up to a fortnight, but what time do you wish?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: On Friday I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So a week would be sufficient --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But a week would be sufficient for your purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, I'm giving you warning at this stage that the ones that haven't been translated by then may well be rejected by the Bench, and you may have to make another application. And the later you're making these applications, the less likely they are to be granted. That's just a general statement, it's not a commitment of the Bench to any response or any decision in relation to these documents. So if we extend that time until a week from today, that gives you a bit more time to deal with your translations, Mr. Cepic, and it enables the Prosecution to make an informed response. The other matter that is related to this is an Ojdanic motion for admission of documents from the bar table which has just been filed on the 16th of October, and that includes 75 untranslated documents. Now, the Bench's inclination, Mr. Sepenuk, in relation to these is to reject them and leave it to you to make another application as and when they're translated. And when you close your case in the -- probably sometime this week, that can be done as it was in relation to the other two accused, subject to the determination of any outstanding issues in relation to documents and the that these had been tendered initially would fall -- would mean that they fell within that category. So without making any final decision on that until you've time to check how long the translations are going to take, I give you an indication that unless they're going to be fairly -- they are fairly imminent, then we are likely to reject these and -- so that time's not wasted in a lot of administrative to-ing and fro-ing over things, that are entirely in your hands. Now, could you try to let us know later today, if possible, or first thing tomorrow when it's likely that these will be translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. So the only formal order we make at this stage is to extend the time for the response to the Lazarevic motion that was filed on the 3rd of October until next Wednesday and expect the Prosecution to respond in relation to the ones for which they have translations. We understand the position in relation to the ones for which you don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Apparently next Wednesday's a holiday, so it will need to be next Tuesday in that case, that's the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I'll be very brief. I feel it incumbent upon me to respond to what has been said. The greatest part of the exhibits of our Defence team was submitted in good time, in June, that is about 1.000 and over exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, this is not getting us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You know you did not respond as quickly as you ought have done to the request to prioritize. If you had done there still may be a problem, I'm not going to dispute that, because of the volume involved. But it's impossible to work out what would have happened if you had been as quick as you ought to have been in relation to the responses. I see no reason, though, to go into that because no decision is going to be taken to exclude documents at this stage. If that question ever arises, you'll have your chance to make appropriate submissions in relation to your position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we can return now to the evidence. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General Professor, if we look at paragraph 3(B) of this combat report of the 354th Combat Brigade, the part dealing with the police is the second paragraph, which begins: [Interpretation] "Our units -- on the territory of Podujevo municipality there have been no activities of any aviational, though intensive reconnaissance is going on. In a small area there is a large number of refugees" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please stop until we finish interpreting the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Relate to the PJP not following the orders of the Crisis Staff in Podujevo. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In the territory of Podujevo municipality there have been no activities of any aviational, though intensive reconnaissance is going on. In a small area there is a large number of refugee which necessitates better food supplies. The treatment of the Siptar population by the VJ is fair. In the area of responsibility of our unit, there are deployed PJP units that do not comply with orders and decisions of the Crisis Staff of the Podujevo Municipal Assembly. We need information who is responsible for them and who commands them." [In English] That's a bit more than I actual said, but I don't think it matters, it gives a bigger picture in front of the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, based on your understanding of the operation of the Law of Defence, Crisis Staffs ought not to have any role under Article 17 in issuing orders to the PJP of the MUP, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if you allow me, I want to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crisis Staffs should have been informed when such units or any other armed unit arrived. The Crisis Staff, in principle, should be aware what that unit is and to whom it is subordinated; if they didn't know that, it's no wonder they're asking. It's true what you said, the command staff of such units was not duty-bound to report to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Same holds true.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the sake of the transcript, 45, 11, I think we all heard that I said that we're talking about the PJP, the JSO but the same holds true for the same and the answer is whoever it is. So I think that clears up the record. General, we have several other documents of a similar nature that I'm not going to go through with you, we'll probably submit them from the bar table once we have translations. I'd like to now move briefly to another topic, your report deals specifically with the structure of the MUP at paragraphs 81 to 87 of your report you discuss the MUP. And in paragraph 82 you state that the Ministry of the Interior has two departments, public and state security, and within the departmental administration of these departments were secretariats of the interior, also known as SUPs, also departments of the interior, also known as OUPs. First of all, would you be surprised or would you agree with me that the -- that the RDB, the State Security Service, did not have any connection to SUPs and OUPs, but rather had CRDBs, centres of the state security department in very -- and detachments of state security department in various locations?
